What these figures do not say

Every page here shows figures the city printed, and every one of them has edges: a schedule that stops short, a total the city's own book contradicts, a classification that is ours rather than theirs. Those are collected here in full, so the pages that draw the money can say them in a line and point at this one. Nothing on this page is a hedge; each is a specific thing a specific document does not do.

50 caveats across 29 published documents, in 7 kinds. Open one to read it in full. A caveat is repeated in each section that lists it.

The kinds

Where the city's own books disagree (6)
Two of the city's pages print different figures or labels for the same thing, by anything from a dollar to hundreds of thousands. This site draws one as printed and says which; it corrects neither.
What isn't in the picture (18)
Money or columns a schedule doesn't carry, or that this site reads and doesn't draw. A total here can be smaller than one printed elsewhere for that reason alone.
Don't add or compare these (5)
Figures that look as if they should be added together or set side by side, and should not: the same dollars shown twice, or two different measures under similar names.
Not every year is the same kind of number (8)
Actual, revised, adopted, projected and unaudited columns measure different things. A change from one to another isn't growth.
Where this site, not the city, decided (7)
A label, a grouping or a classification this site chose to draw the city's figures. The figures are printed; these choices are ours.
What we checked and found to agree (2)
Not limits: places where one schedule was held against another and they agree.
For anyone using the data files (4)
Only matters if you add up the figures in a downloaded file. No page draws them this way.

On At a glance

Where the city's own books disagree

The budget book prints two different totals for Internal Service Funds spending; this chart draws the summary page's.

Internal Service Funds spending is drawn at $26,544,515, which is what pp.66-67 print for FY2027 adopted. Other schedules in the same book make it $26,294,515: pp.75, 183, 205 and 209 print that figure, and p61 prints $26,906,515, which is that figure plus the $612,000 transfer to the CIP it prints beside it, and the 78 rows of pp.85-125 add up to it. The difference is $250,000, in a single Services & Supplies row. This chart keeps the summary page's figure because the Services & Supplies figure that would bring pp.66-67 into line with the other schedules is printed on no page of the book, and every figure here is one the city printed.

About fund-group/internal-service in fy2027-adopted.json (sankey-2027).

What isn't in the picture

Transfers in and transfers out are two separate totals here, and they need not match.

FY 2025-26 adopted: This chart draws the money the city's funds move to one another as two totals, Transfers In and Transfers Out, without pairing each payment with its receipt; Transfers In opens into Budget Book p76's fund-by-fund list. Transfers out ($59,612,734) exceed transfers in ($21,525,997) by $38,086,737. The difference is what the operating funds send to capital projects, the Capital Improvement Program, which Budget Book p222 lists fund by fund; those capital funds are not on this chart.

Don't add or compare these

A department here is not the division of the same name elsewhere; don't add them.

Budget Book pp.85-125 print two blocks per page: spending by DIVISION above, and each DEPARTMENT's funding sources below. Five names are both a department and a division beneath it: City Council, City Manager, City Attorney, General Services and Administrative Services. A mark here is the whole department across every fund; a mark of the same name on the General Fund's breakdown is one division of it.

Link to this caveat

Some fund groups carry money that no single fund's own page prints.

FY 2025-26 adopted: Budget Book pp.66-67 print each fund group's change in balance as one figure. Where some of a group's funds draw on their balances and others add to them, that figure is the net of the funds' changes, which no single fund carries, so for 3 fund groups each group's net is drawn on a box of its own. A fund of such a group is drawn with what it takes in and spends, so its in and out differ by its own change in balance; its details show its two printed balances from pp.186-209 and the change between them. Where pp.66-67 print more for a group than its funds' pages do, the difference sits on the same box, and the box's note says why.

What we checked and found to agree

Click into any part of the citywide chart and the pages it opens into add back up to it, to the cent.

Each part of the citywide chart opens into the finer pages of the budget book that break it down: revenue lines (pp.127-140), funds, General Fund divisions (pp.167-170), spending categories (pp.167-183) or departments (pp.85-125), transfers (p76 and p222) and fund balances (pp.186-209). Added up, they equal the citywide figures on pp.66-67. A box marked derived holds money a page prints for a group and no finer page breaks down.

Shipped inside fy2026-adopted.json (expansion), fy2027-adopted.json (expansion-2027).

Not every year is the same kind of number

Actual, revised and adopted are different kinds of number, so no growth rate is given across them.

FY2023-24 is money that actually moved, FY2024-25 is a mid-year re-forecast, and the two later years are plans adopted together. Each column says which it is; growth from one kind to another is not published, because it would not mean anything.

No page states these: they are about adding up a downloaded file.

In this file an opened box repeats its members' links, so adding every link counts money twice.

FY 2025-26 adopted: An opened node draws a link to each of its members. The General Fund's link to each division totals the rows drawn beyond it; every other node's repeats each link arriving at the member, or leaving it where the node takes nothing in, with the same figure and facts. A remainder cites the members it is the difference of. So 369 printed figures sit behind more than one link, and summing every value_cents in this file counts them more than once.

Shipped inside fy2026-adopted.json (expansion).

FY 2026-27 adopted: An opened node draws a link to each of its members. The General Fund's link to each division totals the rows drawn beyond it; every other node's repeats each link arriving at the member, or leaving it where the node takes nothing in, with the same figure and facts. A remainder cites the members it is the difference of. So 392 printed figures sit behind more than one link, and summing every value_cents in this file counts them more than once.

Only the General Fund's spending is broken down by division; other funds go straight to categories.

Budget Book pp.167-170 break the General Fund's spending down by division, then by category. pp.173-183 print every other fund by category alone, so those funds are drawn straight to their categories. Revenue and spending come from different pages and need not balance fund by fund: a fund with printed revenue and no printed spending is drawn with money arriving and none leaving, and the other way round.
